physics_goals.quote: We report on a precision measurement of low-mass muon pairs in 158 AGeV indium-indium collisions at the CERN SPS.
physics_goals.value: Precision measurement of low-mass muon pairs and J/psi in indium-indium collisions to study the properties of dense matter

summary.plain: NA60 was a CERN experiment that measured pairs of muons from indium-indium collisions with a vertex detector placed close to the target. It found a strong broadening of the rho meson and extra J/psi suppression in collisions with many participants, following up NA50.
summary.technical: NA60: muon spectrometer (inherited from NA50) combined with a silicon-pixel vertex telescope in a dipole magnet in the SPS North Area; precision dimuon spectroscopy in In-In collisions at 158A GeV (2003) and p-A runs at 400 and 158 GeV (2004): 360000 dimuons isolating the thermal excess and the rho spectral function (broadening, no shift), and J/psi suppression beyond cold nuclear matter above ~80 participants.
